artists.biography:
Porcupine Tree are a rock band formed by Steven Wilson in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, England. Their music is associated with both psychedelic rock and progressive rock, yet having been influenced by trance, krautrock and ambient due to Steven Wilson and Richard Barbieri's penchant for the Kosmische Musik scene of the early 1970s, led by bands such as Tangerine Dream, Neu! and Can. Since the early 2000s (decade), their music has been leaning towards progressive metal and alternative rock.
The band is noted for its multimedia approach, with its live performances including screens displaying a different film projection to each song. This visual element was introduced during the tour for the In Absentia album, when the band started to work with Danish photographer and filmmaker Lasse Hoile. This involvement created a distinctive image for the band.
Despite being signed to both Roadrunner and Atlantic labels, the band has their own record label, Transmission, which they use to launch some independent releases and special editions of their albums. In 2007 the band was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound Album with their album Fear of a Blank Planet and then again in 2010 with The Incident.
Music Radar website placed them amongst "The 30 greatest live acts in the world today" (as of 2010), coming at number 4.

perplexity.description:
Closure/Continuation.Live. Amsterdam 07/11/22 documents Porcupine Tree's return to performing following their 2010 hiatus. Recorded on November 7, 2022, at Amsterdam's Ziggo Dome, this live album and concert film captures the band performing material from their 2022 reunion album Closure/Continuation alongside classic tracks spanning their career. The performance features core members Steven Wilson, Colin Edwin, and Gavin Harrison alongside touring musicians Randy McStine on guitars and Nate Navarro on bass.

The setlist emphasizes the new material while drawing from Porcupine Tree's extensive catalog of progressive rock compositions. The performance includes songs from Closure/Continuation such as "Harridan" and "Of The New Day," paired with established fan favorites including "Trains," "Fear of a Blank Planet," and "Anesthetize." The concert presentation incorporates psychotropic visuals that complement the band's intricate instrumental arrangements and atmospheric soundscapes characteristic of their progressive rock style.

Released in December 2023 across multiple formats—2CD/2BD deluxe edition, Blu-ray/DVD, and 4LP vinyl boxset—the recording serves as both a documentation of the band's successful reunion and a testament to their enduring influence within progressive rock. The live performance demonstrates the technical precision and compositional depth that defined Porcupine Tree's original run, presenting their material as what Wilson described as "no hits," treating each song as an anthem in its own right.
